decision: Use Smooth Cayenne as the primary pineapple production variety.
Target 40,000 to 50,000 plants per hectare under the protocol. Actual density today is about 26,500/ha; the earlier 25,000/ha working figure is superseded.
Use peanuts as a principal rotation crop before replanting pineapple.
rationale: Biological nitrogen fixation, residue return, crop-cycle break, possible weed/soil benefits.

decision: Prefer peanut harvest practices that leave roots/nodules in the soil and return vegetative biomass rather than burning it.
Sort pineapple planting materials by type and size before planting.
rationale: Improves uniformity, fertilizer response, forcing timing, and harvest synchronization.

decision: Use harvest data and plant measurements to close the agronomic feedback loop.
Continue evaluating potassium chloride (0-0-60) because a June 2026 harvest appeared larger than older harvests.
Calamansi is agronomically possible on the farm's clay loam if drainage is managed; ~5x5 m spacing was the rainfed working recommendation.
Develop water-security options around storage, pumping, deep-well and/or ram-pump concepts.
Aim for larger fruit in general, because the economics work better as the harvest tends toward primera.
rationale: A higher primera share lifts revenue per fruit more than the extra time in the ground costs. Still active, and the protocol serves it: the 2.7 kg forcing weight exists to produce the larger fruit this decision asks for.

decision: Superseded by the protocol (1 Nov 2026). The forcing threshold is no longer a D-leaf length judged per plot: the protocol forces on plant weight — average at least 2.7 kg, 85% of plants at or above it, lightest at least 2.2 kg, none above 3.3 kg. D-leaf height is reference only.
rationale: The D-leaf readings this decision rested on were taken by a method the farm's consultants have since corrected, and have been set aside.
